name: escher_handlayout_kit
notes: In PROMPT.md: KIT_DIR = toolkit (read-only), INPUT_MAP = draft.escher.json, OUT_DIR = . (the work folder), SPEC = specs/draft.layout.json. The commands written `python run.py ...` there are run with the tool run_toolkit (its arguments after run.py, e.g. ["start", "--input", "draft.escher.json", "--out", "specs/draft.layout.json"]); leave out --name, so that the map of a build is build_N/draft.escher_handlayout.json (the `output:` line): submit the best build's map. Begin with inspect, start and build_0 (PROMPT.md Step B): start already arranges the subsystems and connects them through shared metabolites (a cycle redrawn as a ring, the backbone as a straight column), so build_0 is a connected first map. It is a floor, not a design: improve it, and redraw subsystems (new coordinates for the nodes of a block) where the build reports long lines or area excess. Change the spec with patch: its --json argument is one string, so nothing needs quoting. After every build do what its last line says: while it says NOT FINISHED, go on and do not submit. A reply without a tool call ends the job, so never end a reply with a next step you only announce: make its calls in the same reply. If a build reports unconnected subsystems, connect them first, one per build, with the merge the last line names (move the block next to its partner first); a map of unconnected subsystems is not a result. Do not use --no-pack. The spec's node and reaction ids are strings of digits such as "66" (never BiGG ids such as "pyr_c"); node_names and name in the spec say what they are. Everything you read stays in the chat, which has a limit: read analysis/arrangement.md, the two named sections of analysis/analysis.md, the spec and toolkit/escher_handlayout/agent/prompts/format_reference.md; look things up in toolkit/docs/GUIDE.md; do not read draft.escher.json, the schema, the worked example completely, or the toolkit's .py files. Keep PLAN.md and DECISIONS.md short (tables and lists, no prose). The map's subsystems (the title labels) are the zones and blocks of the start spec.
